title: Unfortunately the package arrived with top corner of the book ...
text: I was really looking forward to receiving this specific edition. I have been saving up for a while to buy it because the cover art is stunning, and I have heard wonderful things about the binding quality from other reputable retailers. However, the experience I had with this particular shipment was deeply disappointing and felt like a complete waste of time and money. Unfortunately, the package arrived with the top corner of the book severely crushed. It is not just a small dent; the corner is bent inward, the cardboard is cracked, and the dust jacket is torn right at the hinge. For a brand new item that I paid full price for, this level of carelessness is unacceptable. I know shipping damages can happen, but usually, sellers are quick to offer a replacement or a refund. In this case, I have to reach out to customer service, fill out forms, and wait for instructions. Why should the customer bear the inconvenience of a poorly packaged product? It makes me question if the warehouse team even cares about what they are sending out. I really wanted to give this five stars because the story itself seems incredible based on the first few chapters I managed to read before the binding refused to lay flat. But you cannot enjoy a book when you are constantly worried about damaging it further. The frustration of dealing with returns overshadows any enjoyment of the content itself. I hope the next reader has better luck, but for me, this was a letdown. I would prefer to see better packaging standards enforced before shipping items out. Do not expect the pristine condition advertised on the main product page if you order from this seller. It is a shame because the literary content is likely fine, but the physical object is ruined upon arrival.

text:
Chariton explores a number of questions revolving around the tragedy of Alamo. Generally I agree with Chariton's deductions although I also believe that all testimony regarding the Zuber must regarded with extreme suspicion. Zuber claimed that he got his information from Louis Rose, the supposed only deserter from Alamo. In a manner resembling Thucidides, Zuber admitted embellishing [making up] Travis' final speech to the troops, including the famous 'line in the sand'. In my opinion, if Zuber lied about anything, then it should be rightfully assumed that he lied about everything.

I think Zuber's testimony is an insult to all the men who died at Alamo. Their heroism stands by itself and required no second hand editorialism. I'll go even further than that to proclaim my own belief that Louis Rose--if he ever existed--never testified to Zuber. Zuber made up the entire story 'whole-cloth'.

Ron

title: Thin
text:
I wish I could give this product zero stars because it genuinely disappointed me on multiple levels. I bought the "Thin" line of dietary supplements with high hopes, expecting a subtle, perhaps unnoticeable shift in my lifestyle that would lead to results. Instead, I found myself dealing with a product that felt more like a placebo with a premium price tag attached to it. From the moment I opened the bottle, the quality was questionable. The capsules had a strange, overly powdery texture that suggested poor manufacturing standards, which immediately put me on edge regarding the actual ingredients inside.

The marketing claims were aggressive, promising noticeable thinning of fat layers within weeks without rigorous exercise or dietary changes. Let me be clear: there was nothing noticeable. I followed the instructions precisely, taking the recommended dosage every single day for four weeks. During this time, I also monitored my caloric intake and maintained my usual activity levels, so any change should have been detectable. There was none. In fact, I felt slightly more bloated in the mornings, which was the opposite of the intended effect.

Customer service was equally frustrating. When I reached out to ask if this was normal, I received a generic, automated response that offered no real solution or explanation. It felt like they were just trying to silence a complaint rather than address a potential issue with the batch. I checked online forums and found several other users reporting the same lack of efficacy, which confirms that this isn’t just bad luck on my part.

The cost is another major factor. For the price of one bottle, I could have purchased a gym membership for two months or hired a nutritionist for a consultation. Those resources would have likely yielded better, healthier, and more sustainable results than this overhyped supplement. It is clear that the brand is spending more on advertising than on effective formulation. I do not recommend this to anyone looking for genuine health improvements. Save your money and invest in whole foods and physical activity instead. This product is a waste of cash and time, and I will not be repurchasing it under any circumstances.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I picked this up on a whim, mostly because the description promised to cut through the noise of modern political discourse, and I am so glad I did. As someone who generally finds political theory dry and overly academic, I was surprisingly hooked from the very first chapter. The author has a rare gift for taking complex, tangled concepts and unraveling them with clarity and humor that never feels condescending. It does not feel like reading a textbook; it feels more like having a deep, insightful conversation with a wise friend who genuinely wants you to understand how the machinery of power really works.

What struck me most was the relevance. You might expect a book on politics to feel dated quickly, but the arguments here are timeless. The historical examples are chosen with precision, and the parallels to current events are drawn without being heavy-handed. I found myself pausing often to highlight passages that challenged my own assumptions, which is the sign of truly engaging non-fiction. It forced me to look at recent news cycles with a critical eye rather than just accepting the prevailing narratives. This is not just a book for politicians or academics; it is essential reading for any citizen who wants to participate more meaningfully in their democracy. It has genuinely expanded my perspective and equipped me with better tools to analyze the world around me. If you are looking for a page-turner that also enriches your mind, this is it. Five stars, easily.

title: The kind of book that you'll be reluctant to finish.
text:
Ever since the quality of Elizabeth George's books took a nosedive, I've been searching for another favorite mystery author. I've found her. And interestingly, like Ms. George, Deborah Crombie is an American woman who sets her mysteries in England.

The book has three threads: one is the ongoing romantic relationship between Superintendent Kincaid and his partner, Gemma James. A second is the mystery itself, involving a beautiful woman whose body is found carefully laid out in a park. The third is the genesis of the relationship among some of the characters/suspects and their families, a relationship which began back when English children were transported to the countryside to spare them the horrors of the World War II Blitz.

All three themes are handled beautifully. The characters of Duncan Kincaid and Gemma James continue to develop believably throughout this series. (This is, I believe, the sixth Kincaid/James book). The real-life problems and uncertainties they encounter while trying to maintain their family and professional obligations, and leave time for themselves and each other, will strike a believable chord with anyone old enough to have gone through this phase of life. The mystery is complex and unpredictable enough to be challenging but not confusing. The ending is beautiful - it settles both the mystery and the unresolved pain from the events of the 1940's.

If you haven't discovered the Crombie/Kincaid/James series yet, I recommend starting with the first one, "A Share in Death," which was nominated for an Agatha as best first novel of 1993. But I've read all of the first six, and they're all excellent.

title: A shamanic journey
text:
In this seventh instalment of Stoner's (and friends') adventures, Stoner and her business partner Marylou have moved their travel agency from Boston to Shelburne Falls. This small New Age town is perfect for Aunt Hermione's psychic activities and a new start for teacher Gwen, Stoner's life partner. But is seventy-five-year-old Hermione eventually getting old, or is her forgetfulness caused by hungry ghosts trying to steal her soul? It is up to reluctant believer Stoner to take a shamanic journey and save her aunt.

While previously her adventures mostly involved down-to-earth detective work on the side, Stoner is no stranger to shamanic journeying ('Grey Magic') and has even experienced time travel ('Captive in Time'). However she'd rather have a normal day-to-day life even if she feels like something is missing, despite Gwen's devoted love.

'Shaman's Moon' carries the trademark humour and feminist ideas of the Stoner McTavish series, even if no one is perfect. This volume, first published in 1998, is infused with light touches of philosophy and a dose of Native-American spirituality. It is captivating and colourful, and I guess would be pivotal in the series if Sarah Dreher had written more. I believe there is an 8th volume ('Love Murders'), but it is out of print or unavailable.

Sadly the author died in spring 2012. I'll be forever grateful to Sarah Dreher for creating one of my favourite fictional characters: the neurotic –but lovable, and forever hypothesizing too much, Stoner McTavish, a womon weary of cats, devoted to her aunt Hermione, passionately in love with her partner Gwen, and generally understanding of her best friend Marylou.

text: We have a large-breed dog (Akita) Rescue and wash lots of dog bowls. We first fell in love with Scrub Daddy because you can use it over and over again with no mildew smell. At first, we were willing to forgive the high price for the little happy face on "daddy" but rather quickly, too quickly, in fact, his face went from happy to sad. In fact, he was downright distraught while sitting on the counter and he flopped around in our hand making it difficult to use. We then stumbled on the Lunatec. Yes, it's a little different. Like a dish cloth but ...more...nylon-netty and flimsy. But that's what makes it perfect! The Luncatec can lay across a finger tip and wipe inside a water bottle or other small area, lay flat and wash out a large water trough or bowl, or, fold it in half or quarters for a scrub-pad effect. A Scrub Buddy, with average use (used twice a day on 6 bowls) lasted about 2 weeks. So far, the Lunatec has been here and after nearly 3 weeks, shows ZERO signs of wear. No smell, no scudge, no bacteria. Just clean, clean, scrubbing and clean clean bowls. Oh, we noted another reviewer was unhappy with the Lunatec because he said he washed out a bowl with bread dough and it clogged the Lunatec. Well, duh, or, should we say "Doh!" You should expect that result with ANY type of sponge or cloth and a gooey/gummy dough. When we make bread or macaroni and cheese and have gooey bowls, we use plastic pan scrapers or a hard sink brush to knock off all the gooey/gummy stuff first and then use a sponge or cloth to do the washing/sanitizing. One Scrub Daddy for $8.50 or FOUR (4) Lunatec's for $7.50. The choice is simple, we think. This product stands up, does MORE than it should, and for that, we love you, you Lunatec!

With these, I do need to take a little extra care mixing on my pallette, and also smooth out the cake of paint in the pan if using it on the brush directly. It handles a bit like a thicker type of paint because of the flake.

I like using them in skies or on water surfaces to add a little extra gleam and luminosity, so I tend to thin them out a good deal and.mix with other colors. They hold up well and blend well without losing their sparkly quality combined with other paints.

I also have the box of various blacks,and experimented mixing these with those on the page and ended up with profoundly 'velvety' luminousity. Like a photo of a velvet dress or curtain. Lovely. I will be buying more of these when they run out, which probably won't be anytime soon... They are large 2cm x 3 xm pans, about half full, for a total of 4-5 mm depthof driet paint. They do not stay sticky like sugar based or gumarabic based binders. The pans are firm and tackless when dry. Would highly recommend.

text:
I am absolutely devastated by this purchase. I spent nearly three hundred dollars on what was marketed as a premium, high-fidelity wireless speaker system, expecting a solid build and crisp sound quality. Instead, I received a lightweight, plasticky disaster that feels like it would break if you looked at it too hard. The packaging was already damaged when it arrived, suggesting it had been thrown around by multiple handlers before even reaching my doorstep, but I was naive enough to think it might still work. It did not work.

From the moment I took it out of the box, everything was wrong. The charging port was loose, wiggling inside the casing with the slightest touch, making it impossible to charge without finding a very specific, awkward angle. The Bluetooth connection was unstable from day one. It would connect for about thirty seconds before dropping the signal entirely, forcing me to reset the device and start the pairing process all over again. This happened multiple times a day, every day, for the two weeks I attempted to use it.

The sound quality is another major letdown. For the price point, I expected clear highs and deep bass. What I got was a muddy, tinny mess that distorted the moment you turned the volume above fifty percent. There is zero bass response, making music sound flat and lifeless, while the highs are painfully shrill after just an hour of listening. It is fatiguing to use.

I contacted customer support three times. Each time, I was given a generic response telling me to restart the device or update the firmware, neither of which resolved the fundamental hardware defects. There is no warranty information included in the box, no manual, and no clear way to initiate a return. I feel like I have thrown my money into a black hole. Do not buy this product. It is a cheaply made, defective waste of resources that I deeply regret owning. If you value your time and your money, save yourself the headache and look elsewhere.

Totally possible, but I do have a strong visual arts background...but photography seems to play be different rules and it was not clear from this book what they are).

title: Love it--a really fun read!
text:
I try really hard to not rehash the entire story or give a bunch of spoilers when I review a book, but it may be hard not to this time! I'll do my best, though. ;)

I received this book to rebiew from the Shut Up & Read group's Read It & Reap event. I have to say, I have been extremely fortunate in the books I've been given to review through them so far. There really haven't been any misses. :)

Anyway, about this book...

I admit it--halfway into the very first chapter I was convinced I was going to hate this book. Liora seemed like the typical, overly-angsty teenager often depicted in paranormal fantasy these days. I initially found her constant whiny and hating herself grating. All I can say is I'm so happy I read chapter 2!

Lucky kicks ass! There's really no other way to describe her. The demon half of Liora who takes over at night, separated from Liora by a curse, she is angry, obviously. And that anger is often turned toward Liora, her fully human side. She is also strong, practical, loyal to her friends, and more willing to look into herself and face the things that make her uncomfortable that she admits. And as time went by, I found Liora to be less annoying as she found her own strength and started to face her own inner "demons".

There are only a couple of things that prevented me from giving this book five stars. The first is that I felt like the romance between Keiran and Liora/Lucky felt too conveniently done to me. There didn't seem to be any build up to it at all. The second issue is that conversations sometimes felt stilted to me. While I appreciate that there was a distinct lack of inappropriate idioms throughout, the almost complete lack of contractions often made discussions feel too formal and unnatural.

This book had everything--romance, fear, growth, drama, excitement, sadness, and victory. It was a great story and I can't wait to read the next one!

title: A fun political satire and much more…
text:
The First Lady Escapes is obviously a satire of the current political atmosphere, but it is also an enjoyable, well thought-out story with a fun cast of characters. As I was reading the story, I found myself falling in love with several of them, especially Angel, the gay Mexican hairdresser, and Moon, a FLOTUS impersonator, and I was eagerly anticipating what would happen as each new chapter began. The short chapters are titled with a location and time to add to the fun so the reader can feel the excitement build as events unfold simultaneously at the White House and across the US and Mexico.

While the President is the focus of the political satire, FLOTUS and the characters who become part of her journey are well-developed and bring the story to life. The detailed descriptions of their surroundings and activities made me feel like I was escaping to Mexico with FLOTUS or part of the White House luxury being experienced for the first time by FLOTUS’ impersonator.

I picked up this book because I was intrigued by the premise and hoped for a few moments of escapism from the daily news. I got that and so much more. The author acknowledges the current political situation inspired her to write this satire, but beyond that initial premise, she created an entertaining story with well developed characters that evolve to show the people behind traditional stereotypes whether they are immigrants, paparazzi, or transgender. This is definitely not a read for supporters of the current administration. But for everyone else who has felt concern, frustration, or outrage as they read the latest news feeds, this book will put a smile on your face and even let you laugh out loud and be entertained for a few fun hours.

title: When Simple Faith is Simply Not Enough
text:
"Today, twenty-first century theology tends to make religion a belief based upon faith rather than a belief of faith based upon fact. History, science, and conflicting Scriptures are all too often dismissed when they conflict with accepted creeds or dogma. Most Judeo-Christians are taught there are certain areas of their religion they should not question, causing the phrase “it is a matter of faith” to be well-worn and overused.
Scripture encourages individuals to question their idea of God."
And question it she did!
For Jodell Onstott, like so many of us, simple faith was simply not enough. Unable to dismiss the passionate; yet, conflicting views of countless denominations… the seemingly endless interpretations of a single text… the bearing of historic facts and archeological discoveries… the consequence of scientific evidences… Jodell embarked upon a decade long mission to discover the not so simple truth. And though the title of the subsequent book, “YHVH Exists” may eliminate the suspense of her ultimate conclusion, Jodell’s journey is a masterpiece of well-organized testimonies and closely examined proofs. Leaving no stone unturned, her systematic examination of the data demonstrates a sincere desire to reach an objective opinion.
The long-awaited “YHVH Exists” is a thorough and fascinating study that will challenge your most hidden preconceptions, and, may well find itself on the more than one bestseller’s list in the process.

For anyone on the fence, do yourself a favor and buy this copy. Whether you are a devoted fan of literary fiction or just looking for a gripping page-turner, this book delivers on all fronts. text: I purchased this for a long trip from VA to VT. I wanted to talk on the phone if needed, and do it hands free. This works great, as I had no Bluetooth in my 08 Nissan Altima. It only works through your car speakers when you have the radio on AUX input. This wasn't a problem on a long trip, as I had thousands of songs on my Samsung Galaxy S5 to listen to. I could listen to my music, skip songs when I wanted by pushing a button, and when a call came in all I had to do was say "answer" or push a button to accept the call. When the call ends, the music picks back up where it left off. To make a call, I could do it by voice (call Tina at home) or use the phone to dial it manually. It then stops the music and dials who you are calling. It doesn't work unless you have your car radio on AUX. You can't use the actual radio and use the SoundBot at the same time. It comes with a 12v plug (cigarette lighter plug) that has 3 USB outlets on it. One of those is used for the SoundBot, the other 2 can be used for GPS, phone charger, etc. Then there is a 3.5mm plug that goes to the AUX input on your radio. Your phone then connects wirelessly through Bluetooth to the SoundBot. I used my GPS on my phone, and the directions was heard through my car speakers over my music I was playing through my phone. I made and received many calls on my trip, and everybody said they heard me loud and clear. Great price on the SoundBot, and I loved it. I can't use it when listening to my local radio stations at home, but if I have it plugged in and connected, I can push the AUX button on my radio and use it then to talk. title: Sweet, slow, sad
text:
Thin Wood Walls follows young Joe Hanada's family experiences during the time of WWII. After the bombing of Pearl Harbor, Joe's father is taken away by the FBI as a person of suspicion because he is a community leader. The rest of the family, including Joe's feisty grandmother and more feisty big brother Mike, are taken to Tule Lake Relocation Camp and must adjust to a new life while anxiously awaiting the return of the father.

Not much happens in the book, as camp life is boredom, waiting, hoping, but Joe tries to make do and make sense of what is happening while fearing what his big brother intends to do. The story is balanced, showing how not all white Americans were against the Japanese in the U.S. Some Japanese were very angry while many exhibited a sad stoicism. Perhaps what sets this book apart from other internment stories is that it is set in the Tule Lake camp, which was where troublemakers, the "no-no's" and those wanting to return to Japan were sent. This created a turbulent, sometimes dangerous atmosphere that other camps did not experience, at least not on that level. Thin Wood Walls delves into this in a manner suitable for middle-graders.

The book is a bit slow, but sweet, the writing rather plain despite the bits of haiku, but this will appeal to boys as well as girls and provide a thoughtful look at the sad facts of this long-hidden part of U.S. history. Expect a tear at the end, and be sure to read the Author's Notes.

[[ASIN:0939165538 Looking Like the Enemy: My Story of Imprisonment in Japanese American Internment Camps]] is also set in Tule Lake, but is a true story. A Young Reader's edition is coming out in Fall 2010.

text:

When I took him to the vet to have him neutered, they couldn't proceed because they noticed he was short of breath and after listening to his lungs (lots of crackling short breaths & coughing occasionally), doing bloodwork (which was negative for any infection), an X-ray (which didn't show anything) & then giving me antibiotics because she knew something was wrong but couldn't find a reason for his respiratory problems. $375.00 dollars later, I brought home my sick kitten who still wasn't fixed.
Later that day it hit me that this fine, powder like liter might be the cause of his symptoms. After looking up how this fine silica sand could cause respiratory problems, I called my vet, explaining about the cat liter I was using and now his symptoms made sense to her. I too have been having similar respiratory problems (since I had a second litter box near my bed to make sure the kitten didn't have any accidents at night).
Although I had no problems when I only had my two adult cats using this litter, the kitten tended to play with the fine sand and was very thorough when covering offensive odors not just for himself but for the other two cats too. He often had pink sand on his nose, so it's not a big leap that some of it was getting into his lungs.
Just wanted to warn everyone that this litter is not a good choice for kittens. I've switched both cat boxes to fresh step premium crystals, it's a larger, pearl like bb which has no dust and is too big to be inhaled! Hope this helps others whose kittens are short of breath.

text:
I finally decided to treat myself to a proper facial moisturizer after years of neglecting my skin barrier due to stress and harsh weather conditions. The packaging of Where's the apricot? is quite striking, with its minimalist white bottle and simple typography that immediately suggests a clean, clinical approach to skincare. This aesthetic alone was enough to make me confident that I was making a sensible investment in my daily routine. The product arrived quickly and was well-protected, which is always a relief when ordering fragile glass containers online.

Upon opening the bottle, the first thing I noticed was the scent. It has a very distinct, fresh aroma that reminds me slightly of citrus but with a subtle nutty undertone, likely from the apricot kernel oil mentioned on the label. It is not overpowering or perfumed in a way that feels artificial. Instead, it smells natural and inviting, which sets a pleasant tone for my morning skincare ritual. I have combination skin, which means I usually struggle to find a moisturizer that hydrates without making my T-zone look greasy by midday. This product has managed to strike a surprising balance.

I have been using it consistently for about three weeks now. The texture is lightweight and absorbs into the skin relatively quickly, leaving behind a soft, supple finish rather than a heavy, occlusive layer. I noticed a significant improvement in the dryness around my nose and cheeks, areas that usually flare up during colder months. My skin feels more resilient and less reactive to environmental changes. However, I am giving this product four stars instead of five for one specific reason. While the hydration is excellent, I found that for my oily zones, I might need to use a slightly lighter layer or perhaps pair it with a mattifying powder during the day to maintain shine control. It works well, but it requires a bit of adjustment depending on where you apply it on your face.

The ingredients list is transparent and reassuring, focusing on natural oils and gentle botanicals. I appreciate that there are no harsh sulfates or artificial fragrances cluttering the formula. For anyone looking for a straightforward, effective moisturizer that does exactly what it promises without unnecessary gimmicks, this is a strong contender. It is not a miracle worker that will erase years of sun damage overnight, but it is a reliable staple for maintaining healthy, hydrated skin. The price point is reasonable for the quality of the formula, and I expect to repurchase this once I finish the current bottle. It has earned its place on my bathroom shelf as a consistent, trustworthy part of my regimen.

UPDATE 08/12/2018 REPLACED BELT

After about a year of daily use I noticed a black powder accumulating on the ground under the belt cover. I figured out it was the belt wearing out. I purchased a new one (OEM PN 5PK1320). I couldn't find any instructions on the Sunny site but it's not that hard. Remove all the screws from the belt cover, including the one that holds it in place on the left side of the bike. You might have to remove the right pedal to get the cover completely off. Once you have the cover off, remove the 10-mm retaining nuts on the two eyebolts that align the flywheel, then loosen the two 19-mm nuts that hold the flywheel in place. Lift the flywheel far enough up to slip the old belt out and the new belt in. Align the belt on the front pulley and reattach the 10-mm eyebolts to the frame, then tighten the 19-mm flywheel bolts. Place the belt on the back pulley as far as you can get it, then turn the crank to get it on the rest of the way, the same way you get a chain back onto a bicycle chain ring. Put the cover back on and you are done.

title: Best of the pre-PEP or pre-W series works
text:
Perhaps because of a lack of publication or perhaps because of a general lack of distribution of his ideas (Peirce tended to write only for other philosophers and logicians), Peirce's philosophical thinking was not well known until Eisele's "New Elements of Mathematics" (NEM), and the Peirce Edition Project's W series: "The Chronological Writings of Charles Sanders Peirce". Buchler's work is easily the best introduction to the work of Peirce prior to the availability of NEM and the W series.

Buchler worked from an earlier collection of Peirce's writings, called the CP series, consisting of 8 volumes of poorly edited papers presented in such a way as to not show the depth, or originality of his thought, or the evolutionary growth in the depth and power of his thought.

Nevertheless, Buchler's volume is still an excellent, easy to read, and easy to understand (relative to Peirce's depth of thinking) introduction to the immensity of the thought of Charles Peirce. I recommend it as a great reading value.

title: Recommend This Switch Box

After several month's use on my HD flat panel TV, I can easily recommend this box if you need to "fan-out" a single HDMI input port to five independent signal sources. The remote works well and the overall hook-up and operation is simple and straight forward. Overall device quality seemed very good and packaging for shipment was good. I could not detect any added audio or HD video signal deterioration/distortion. The instructions are fairly adequate, just remember to pull the plastic insulating tape out of the back of the remote to allow the battery to make internal electrical contact to start the remote! This was not mentioned in the instruction sheet of the unit I received.

I can understand why some reviewers have complained that the power and selected channel indicator LED's are too bright and are distracting. My solution was to put a 3.5 inch strip of gray electrical tape across the front of the unit. The gray is less obtrusive than the white electrical tape that I tried, and does it a better job of taming the LED's output. You get a diffuse lighted dot to indicate "power on" and the channel that is "on", and can neatly write the name of the signal for the channels on it [e.g. DVD, Fire Stick, Computer, Game, etc.] with a Ultra Fine Point permanent marker pen. Put a 3.5 inch strip of Scotch Magic Mending Tape on top to protect what you have written on the electrical tape if that is a concern.

title: It's not about food
text:
Differently from the movie, this is not a tale about sophisticated food. It deals with the severe restrictions that puritanism imposes on pleasure - and how a tastefull dinner, with the help of some good wines, helps this fundamentalist lutheran aging community to retrieve joy and forgiveness.

In the movie, although the puritan restrictions are present, stress is on the food - the ingredients, the way it is being prepared, the discovery of it by the coachman and Bebette's assitant, and principally the precise description by the general. The transformation of the puritans, from mere tolerance of an extravagance to real appreciation and joy only underines the quality of what is being served.

In the novel, food plays a secondary role, contrasting with the grey sad environment and the equally gray and sad inhabitants of a norwegian community lost in the high north, squeezed between the mountains and an unfriendly see. Stress is on the way a severe pastor has molded the spirit of his daughters and of his few followers, banning all earthly pleasures.

I've decided to read the novel after having a dinner that reproduced the menu of Babette's feast, preceded by the film and a technical explanation by the danish chef. Dinner was excelent and our community did not resemble at all to the inhabitants of the small village - which in the film was moved from Norway to Denmark. I was first surprised by the differences in approach but then I realized that this short novel gives you food for thoughts. While the movie is pure pleasure, the novel is profound.

I recommend it and, if I may suggest, have it complete: the movie, the dinner and the short novel.

UPDATE: April 2016 -- I've been using this pump for a little over a year and the pump, itself, continues to function well but I'm beginning to have problems with the float switch. The switch now turns the pump on in the full off position but, if I raise it I/2 inch, it turns off. It will restart gain at about 1 1/2 inches up or floating. I've managed to keep it working by holding it above the full off position with a rope but I'm now concerned that the rope will float away and the pump will run until it burns up or destroys the battery by running it until it is totally discharged. It appears to find a quality float switch, I'll have to spend about as much for the switch as I have for the switch and pump combo and the add-on pump. I'm still very pleased with the pump. It does what it's supposed to and does it well.

This is a strong pump for its small size and low cost. It took about fifteen minutes to pump out a twelve foot Portabote that was three quarters full of water and it's worked without fail since I installed it to keep the boat rain water free. At just over $20 for the pump and switch with an additional backup pump as a $5 add-on, this is a super bargain. So far both pump and switch have proven to be reliable but they're not designed for heavy duty use and I would not think of using them in situations where the vessel will be unattended for a long period of time or when large volumes of water need to be dealt with. While the pump can clear a significant amount of water quickly, it's really designed for light incidental use. I'm very happy with this purchase because I believe that I'm using the pump and switch as they were intended...in a non-critical situation to handle incidental rainwater and spray. To ask them to do much more could be asking for trouble.

title: a page-turning flash of comic brilliance, comic as in deeply human
text:
The chief delight of this book, and there are many, is that Cunningham has tailored a page-turning, oh-no-don't-do-that!, classic plot of confused identity (i.e. a Comedy of Errors) onto a cutting-edge New York scene, and delivered it with humor, humanity, and depth in a style that is fashionable, highly entertaining, and sexy on the one hand, and deeply poetic on the other, as in he has maybe been reading not only the Bard but that other bard, James Merrill. The characters are sharply drawn both in body and mind, and the plot twists true to both life and character.
Other reviewers are complaining about over-writing. While this may be a bit like grousing that chocolate is rich, Cunningham does stumble here and there, e.g. when he has his hero/narrator say, 'What did Shakespeare say? Our little lives are rounded by a sleep.' This is artificial; Shakespeare himself would have solved the problem by giving that line to the college-student daughter, maybe upon seeing her father drinking vodka in the night!
I think Cunningham has just hit his stride--fine as his past achievements are. Hooray for that! Now lay The Tempest aside, Sir, take up your wand and book, and play, play, play for us!

title: Worst air mattress
text:
I never write negative reviews because I prefer to give people the benefit of the doubt, but this air mattress is absolutely the worst purchase I have made in the last five years. I bought it specifically for a weekend camping trip with my family, thinking it would be a convenient alternative to inflating and deflating sleeping bags every single night. That was a massive mistake. I followed the instructions exactly, using the recommended pump to inflate it to the maximum pressure level indicated in the manual. For the first thirty minutes, it seemed firm enough. I felt confident. However, by the time I actually got into bed, I could already feel a significant loss of support. It did not take long at all for the bottom side to begin drooping, creating a hammock effect that was incredibly uncomfortable and bad for my back.

By the second hour of sleep, I had to wake up multiple times because the mattress was slowly deflating on its own. I checked every seam and valve to ensure it was closed tightly, but there was no leak anywhere. It was just the material itself expanding and failing to hold the air pressure properly. The construction feels incredibly flimsy and cheap. The surface texture is rough and provides almost no grip, so I kept sliding off to one side throughout the entire night. It was a cold, hard, lumpy nightmare. I tried using the electric pump again in the morning to re-inflate it, but it barely went up. I am genuinely shocked that this product is still on the market with such a low rating that hasn't deterred buyers. Do not waste your money on this garbage. If you need an air mattress, save your time and go buy a reputable brand from a well-known manufacturer. This item is essentially trash wrapped in plastic. I threw it in the recycling bin immediately after this trip. It is an insult to customers who pay full price for comfort and reliability. I am extremely disappointed and will never trust this brand again.

title: An amazing emotional roller-coaster of a story.
text:
POSSIBLE SPOILERS AHEAD:

I honestly have to say that it's not only the best book I've ever read but probably one of the greatest pieces of writing I've ever read. From beginning to end, I found myself completely drawn to the story of Jersey City bus driver Andre Bolden.

The book is a real page turner and what really kept me hooked besides wanting to know the story resolution was the relationship between Andre and Sandra, the mother of his son. Sandra had so much resistance towards him that I kept turning pages eager to see if Andre could ever get over that emotional fortress. At the same time, the theme about snitching itself was handled very well by Mr. Mattison without being too imposing about it. Rather than making it about a guy or people around him who don't snitch, it comes across as a story of a man whose wrong choices in life start to eat him up bit by bit, living in the fear of losing his life as he had with getting kicked out of school, losing Sandra, and eventually losing his job. He thinks living back with Sandra and Little Dre would solve all his problems. But what transpires over the course of the book leads Andre to a much higher purpose of standing up for himself and those dearest to him.

I also want to applaud Mr. Mattison himself for being able to write the book using little to no profanity. I'm sure it was quite a challenge to do that given the genre and the tone of the book.

Overall, this is a must read for teenagers and adults across America. Look forward to the movie adaptation.

text:
tl;dr version: For $32 you can't go wrong.

I've been using this backpack cooler almost daily since I bought it two weeks ago. The straps are long and wide enough to be comfortable when wearing this as a backpack, and I'm a pretty big guy. It also carries well slung over one shoulder, which is not always the case.

Some of the reviews fault the zippers for breaking. Yeah, I can see that happening if you jerk them, are impatient, or in a hurry and not paying attention. I've had no problems with them. Same with the stitching; I pack out at about 20 pounds and I've seen no signs of wear and tear, yet. It has only been two weeks, sure, but still...

Pros: keeps food plenty cold for a whole day when used with re-freezable ice packs; lots of room inside, comfortable straps. Netting pockets for water bottles, etc. on the sides are deep and big enough for wide bottles.

Cons: zippered storage compartments on the front and top are inadequate. No "waterproof" storage compartment for keys, phone, etc.

title: A Must-Have
text:
The authors offer truly groundbreaking insights and methods in this book, and I will cite a few, but the depth and breadth of their work is far too vast to encapsulate here. They note the plethora of unhelpful, anecdotal advice that often passes for wisdom in similar books, and instead provide scientifically documented, step-by-step methods for defining and achieving goals. They provide compelling examples of how these techniques have been implemented. The most fascinating story, in my opinion, involved the eradication of the guinea worm, an endemic parasite that can grow up to three feet long and emerges through the skin causing tremendous pain. The authors cited techniques employed by Carter Foundation workers to teach villagers how to filter their water and prevent reinfestation of water sources by infected persons. Carter Foundation workers sought positive deviants (villages who had learned their own ways of avoiding guinea worm infestation) to teach other villages what to do.

I noted many techniques that I myself had discovered by trial and error, such as perfect practice, which involves working on improving specific elements of a task; they cite basketball freethrowing, where perfect practice includes improving followthrough, elbow position, etc., as opposed to results oriented practice that can reinforce poor technique, e.g. shoot until I get 20 baskets. As a Chemistry teacher, I inherently implemented many of these techniques. This book provided me with more insight and concrete guidance than most of the teaching and education books I was provided in my teacher training.

This is one of the most enlightening books I have ever read on human behavior. Having borrowed this book from the library, I now plan to purchase it (the actual ink and paper version), because I know I will refer to it again and again.

Narrated by Eric Conger with dignity and clarity.

title: Missing a heartbeat.
text: Okay--so there's a heartbeat to fiction, any fiction, long or short.  Beat: Exposition.  Beat: Rising Action.  Beat: Climax.  Beat: Falling action.  And in good, thoughtful fiction the falling action revisits the exposition and something has changed about the characters or the circumstances of the conflict--hopefully in all three.  I enjoyed Micah--I did.  He wasn't my favorite character, and now I like him more, and since I intend to continue reading this seminal series, that's a good thing, because he's become a big part of it.  In a way, reading this work was sort of like getting to know a brother in law you thought was just set decoration and finding out he's got a good sense of humor or something.  The problem with the novella was, that Anita, our main character, didn't seem to come to this--or any--conclusion about this character by the end of the story.  I needed to see some sort of reflection about Micah, about her acceptance of him in her life, in her bed, and instead, we jumped out of a (admittedly hot and character, uhm, building) sex scene, and into the metaphysics and although both parts were fun, there was no emotionally satisfying wrap up.  At the end, it was just Micah and Nathaniel and that's it, folks-- he's just set decoration again when we'd really started to think of him as a friend.  I still love this series, and I still like these characters, but this smaller installment was missing something vital.  It was missing a heartbeat.

title: Opened my EYES!
text:
I am writing this review because I feel compelled to share how profoundly this book shifted my perspective, something I haven't experienced in years of reading. As a professional who thought they had seen it all, I approached this title with a healthy dose of skepticism. I expected generic self-help clichés or superficial advice that we all encounter daily. Instead, what I found was a rigorous, beautifully structured argument that challenges the very foundations of how we perceive reality. The author does not just tell you to open your eyes; they provide the logical framework and the psychological tools necessary to actually do so.

The pacing is excellent. There are no filler chapters designed to pad the word count. Every paragraph serves a specific purpose, building upon the last to create a cohesive narrative that feels both personal and universally applicable. I found myself stopping frequently to reflect on my own biases and assumptions, which was an uncomfortable but necessary process. The writing style is accessible without being condescending, striking a rare balance between academic depth and conversational warmth.

What struck me most was the section on cognitive dissonance and how we rationalize our poor decisions. It was a mirror held up to my own life, revealing patterns I had ignored for decades. This is not a quick fix book. It requires active engagement and honest self-reflection. However, the payoff is immense. Since finishing this book, I have noticed a tangible improvement in my decision-making processes and my ability to empathize with people who hold different viewpoints.

If you are looking for entertainment, this might not be it. But if you are seeking genuine growth and a deeper understanding of the human condition, this book is an absolute necessity. It is rare to find a work that feels so urgently important and timeless all at once. I highly recommend it to anyone willing to do the hard work of seeing the truth.

title: Better than the movie, but still one of Marvel's weaker '90s efforts.
text:
A decent tale that works better than the Infinity War movie, especially where the character of Thanos is concerned. Even so, this is far from an impressive story arc, and one that becomes muddled and too crammed with characters for its own good. These kind of stories are also difficult to effectively tell when you have a nigh-omnipotent being involved. Marvel still had some great comics in the early '90s like Gruenwald's run on Captain America and Mark Bagley's artistry on Spider-Man, but this book was a sign of things to come as comic plot lines became so mixed up and convoluted that it hurt the industry so badly Marvel nearly went bankrupt.

The best and most effective Marvel superhero crossover is still the original 12-issue Secret Wars series, released in 1984 (and one that had the most lasting consequences, ie Spider-Man's black suit, the Thing leaving the Fantastic Four, etc). Infinity Gauntlet's worth a read, but fails to deliver in its promised scope, and certainly a tale that isn't, by any means, a pivotal moment in Marvel comicdom.

text: I have struggled for years to find a way to keep my indoor cat, Luna, mentally stimulated and physically active without resorting to cheap plastic toys that fall apart in minutes. The concept is simple but brilliant. You place kibble or small treats inside the rotating compartments. There are no sharp edges, and the pieces lock together securely so Luna cannot accidentally break it while playing. It is also quiet enough that it does not wake me up in the morning, a common issue with other noisy toys. I have recommended this to all my friends with cats. It is an excellent investment in your pet’s well-being and happiness. If you are looking for a way to bond with your cat and encourage healthy eating habits, you cannot go wrong with this product. text: I purchased this set of adhesive hooks with high hopes for organizing my home office, specifically to hang my coffee mug organizer and some lightweight tools above my desk. The concept seemed perfect for avoiding holes in the wall and keeping my workspace clutter-free without needing to drill or use unsightly command strips that often leave marks. The packaging looked professional, and the instructions were clear, promising a bond that lasts for months rather than days. Unfortunately, the reality of using this product was a stark disappointment that I never expected given the positive reviews I had read prior to buying. On the first day of installation, I carefully cleaned the surface of the wall with the provided alcohol wipe, pressed the hook firmly for the recommended thirty seconds, and waited the full hour before hanging anything. I hung a small, lightweight basket filled with pens and paperclips. Within less than four hours, I heard a distinct thud from the corner of my eye. Rushing over, I found the basket on the floor, shards of plastic scattered everywhere, and the adhesive hook lying limp and useless against the baseboard. It had not just failed to hold the item; it had completely detached itself from the wall, leaving no residue but a significant mess. I tried again with a different hook and a slightly heavier bag of tissues. This time, it lasted only six hours before falling again. I understand that surfaces can vary, but claiming a strong bond for months is misleading when the product cannot even survive a standard workday. For the price, I expected basic reliability, not constant cleaning up of dropped items. The adhesive seems weak and inconsistent, with no guarantee that it will stick properly regardless of how well you follow the instructions. If you are looking for a temporary solution for something that absolutely must not fall, this might work for ten minutes, but for any practical, long-term office organization, it is a waste of money. Do not trust the initial stickiness; it is not reliable. I have since switched to traditional command strips, which are more expensive but actually stay on the wall as advertised. Save your time and frustration, and avoid this product entirely.

title: Too many contradictions - sometimes on adjoining pages
text:
I wanted to like this book, despite having read O'Reilly's "Killing Patton" which contained a very thin conspiracy theory about Patton's death. "Legends and Lies" purports to be a history book but is filled with inconsistencies and inaccuracies.

For example, on page 5, the book states that "Daniel Boone was born in Pennsylvania in 1734, the sixth child of ...". Yet on page 6, in a photo apparently depicting an unidentified stone house, the cut says "... Daniel Boone was the seventh of twelve children." Which is it?

On page 67, the narrative talks about Kit Carson being attacked by a band of Kiowa Indians on November 25, 1864. "Within hours, about fourteen hundred warriors attacked. It was similar to the situation in which General Custer would find himself a few months later." But 'Custer's Last Stand' occurred on June 25, 1876, nearly twelve YEARS later, not 'a few months.'

Also on page 67, "... while the Navajos, after signing a treaty in 1868 with General Sherman, were moved to a portion of their traditional lands, where they have remained." But on the photo on the facing page, the cutline says the Navajos "...settled peacefully on this land, as negotiated by (Kit) Carson." But in 1868, Carson was in Colorado, either dead or dying, according to the same chapter.

While any history book might understandably contain discrepencies, when compared to other history books, it should not contradict itself, especially on adjoining pages. For that reason, I stopped reading this book about half-way through and consider it a waste of money.

title: CHEAP and Broken after 3 days!
text:
I am writing this review because I feel completely cheated by my purchase. I ordered this item thinking I was getting a high-quality toy for my child, given the somewhat polished product images on the website. However, the reality is that this is one of the cheapest, flimsiest pieces of plastic I have ever encountered. The moment I opened the box, I could tell something was wrong. The packaging was torn and taped shut with cheap duct tape, which already raised some red flags, but I hoped for the best. The item itself felt lightweight and hollow, lacking the solid construction I expected from a premium toy.

On the first day, everything seemed okay, or at least passable. My kid played with it for a few hours without any immediate issues, though I noticed several loose seams along the edges. I didn’t think much of it, assuming it would settle in. That was my mistake. By the end of the second day, a small crack had appeared near the main hinge mechanism. I tried to gently press it back into place, warning my child to be careful, but I had no idea how fragile the material actually was. Then, yesterday, exactly three days after I received it, the toy completely broke apart. The main structural piece snapped clean off while my son was simply holding it.

It did not fall; it was not dropped; it just disintegrated from normal handling. This is not durability; this is a complete failure of product quality. I have bought much cheaper toys before that lasted for years, and this item cost more than half of those, yet it has already become trash. I tried to contact customer service, but the response time is slow, and I fear they will blame user error, which is absurd. I cannot recommend this to anyone. If you are looking for something that will actually last through playtime, avoid this at all costs. You are throwing your money away on a product designed to break immediately. I am deeply disappointed and will never buy from this seller again. The lack of basic integrity in the materials is unacceptable for a toy meant for children. Save your money and look elsewhere for a better, safer, and longer-lasting option.

Held Evans' honesty about her Evangelical upbringing, conversational tone, willingness to take many of the Biblical guidelines to their literal extreme, and inclusion of how she and her husband felt about many of the experiences invites the reader to enter into the story both to observe her actions and explore one's own views on what it means to be a "biblical woman." title: Great whimsies in an otherwise standard puzzle
text:
This one's all about the whimsies. The pieces and border are strip-cut standard **yawn**. The picture blends gently from one piece to another, making it difficult to see the whole thing until you have most of the puzzle together (unless you use the box picture, which I never do). For quite a while, I thought I was doing just another bland puzzle that happens to be made of wood, and then finally, starting past the halfway point and all the way through completion, the whimsies took shape. And that's where this puzzle gets its value. The shaped pieces are fun, cleverly placed, and at least one got me laughing. They are good enough to win back most of the points, and I'll end up doing the puzzle again at times (though it won't ever be my favorite).
All-in-all, this one redeems itself via whimsies, and don't expect exciting pieces or a cool border otherwise. If classic-shape jigsaw pieces and straight borders are your preference, you may even really like this one.
As usual for me, a point is deducted for: splinter-tastic cheap wooden box and amateurish, minimalistic labeling. Artifact is a great puzzle maker and deserves better than both.

title: A Classic with a contemporary interpretation
text:
Not much needs to be said here about the story of this truly perennial classic. The War of the Worlds (1898) is the account of Martians invading earth, attacking and ruining London. What happens to the rest of earth and mankind is not resolved till the very end. Although this novel was seen as the start of modern science fiction, it had also a deeper meaning of fighting tyrannies and the occurrence of mass-hysteria.

This deeper meaning was clearly shown when Orson Wells broadcast in 1938 an extremely believable radio dramatization. Listeners thought that Martians were actually attacking and in panic they left their homes trying to escape this terrifying experience. It is interesting to note that that broadcast happened at the eve of World War II.

Now in 2005, a new movie adaption has just been released by Steven Spielberg and starring Tom Cruise. While I'll leave it to movie critics to evaluate that movie, it has already received wide acclaim for its special effects. Something else interesting to note is that in the early scenes of the attack by the Martians, the children of the character played by Cruise question whether these are attacks by "terrorists". In an era where we are sandwiched in time by 9/11, the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, and further terrorist attacks in Bali, Istanbul, Madrid and London, the world seems again in the grip of fear, of wars and of mass-hysteria. One could wonder if The War of the Worlds in 2005 again will create or foresee further scares in the world.

What makes this edition of The War of the Worlds so worthwhile is not just the inclusion of the classic illustrations by Henrique Alvin Correa, but also the introduction by Robert Bartholomew. Bartholomew is a leading expert on panic attacks, media manipulation and mass delusion, and he puts this book in historical and contemporary context. He tries to answer why this book has "created" such a scare in 1898, in 1938 and maybe again in 2005, or is the scare in all of us us calling this book into everlasting existence? I rate this edition 4 stars, and just wished that the publisher had considered releasing a hard cover edition.

And also, what annoys me, is that she refers to Christian "wanting to hurt her." she knew the terms of their engagement and also, she knew of the lifestyle Christian was into (He gave her more than enough warning). At some point, you stop questioning and start accepting. That never happens with Ana. She's so fickle it's wholly vexatious. Ana does portray a real, genuine personality, I can attest to that. I know of several girls who are just like her, annoyingly innocent and fickle in their relationships. title: Better respected than loved.
text:
"The Morels", a debut novel by Christopher Hacker, is one of those novels that can be described as better respected than loved. The story - a story within a story - is the tale of how a bunch of bad decisions have affected the lives of at least three generations of one family - the Morels - and those of people tangentially connected with them.

Arthur Morel, a musical prodigy, only child of divorced parents has walked through life in seeming non-connection with the realities we all have to deal with. After a particularly beautiful musical recital, the teenaged Arthur has performed an on-stage act of defilement that has stunned and revolted his audience. The years pass, Arthur has met, married a young woman called Penelope, and fathered a son, Will, with her. Penelope supports the family as a pastry chef while Arthur continues to "dabble" with life. He publishes a well-received novel and is in the process of finishing his second novel, called "The Morels", when Christopher Hacker's book begins. The story Hacker tells is narrated by a young man - himself adrift in movie making - who had known Arthur as the young defiler and now moves back into Arthur's life. He acts as teller of Arthur's story and its major interpreter.

"Interpreted" because there are a lot of actions which need to be interpreted to both those affected by the actions and those merely standing-by, observing. Are a man's possible incestuous thoughts always acted on - or can they merely remain, safely, thoughts? Where do lies and truth-telling become hopelessly meshed until neither is recognisable? In a broad way, Hacker's book is a bit like "The Dinner", by Herman Koch, another book where families and lies are tossed together and the truth never quite emerges.

Christopher Hacker's book should make the reader think about truth and lies and that muddy middle in between. Arthur, Penelope, and Will Morel are victims of both lies and truth, which they, themselves, perpetrate. It's an interesting book.

title: Could have been better
text:
I picked this book up largely based on the glowing descriptions in the catalog, hoping for a deep dive into the subject matter. Unfortunately, my experience with it was a mix of high hopes and eventual disappointment. The initial chapters are engaging enough, and the author has a pleasant writing style that makes the early pages flow smoothly. It feels like a genuine attempt to explore complex ideas in an accessible way, which I appreciate. However, as the book progresses, the depth fades significantly.

I found myself skimming through several chapters because the arguments felt repetitive and lacked the substantive evidence promised in the introduction. It is frustrating to invest time in a narrative that seems interested more in filling space than providing insight. For anyone looking for a comprehensive overview or a rigorous analysis, this title falls short. It stays surface-level for too long, missing the opportunity to offer a truly transformative perspective on the topic.

That said, it is not entirely without merit. If you are a casual reader who just wants something light to pass the time during a weekend, this might suffice. The layout is clean, and the font size is comfortable for long reading sessions. But if you are a serious student or enthusiast of the genre, you will likely feel let down by the lack of original thought and the reliance on clichéd conclusions. I expected more from the publisher given the hype surrounding the release. I would hesitate to recommend this to anyone seeking genuine intellectual stimulation. It feels like a cash-grab rather than a meaningful contribution to the field. There are better resources available for those who want to truly understand the nuances of this subject. Save your money and look for a more detailed work elsewhere.

text: I have been on the hunt for a portable air compressor that can keep up with my weekend hobby of inflating paddleboards, inflatable kayaks, and even the occasional car tire in a pinch. I was able to fully inflate a large stand-up paddleboard in under three minutes, which is incredibly fast compared to my old manual foot pump that took twenty minutes and made me sweat. The motor sounds robust, not like those cheap plastic toys that whine and die after a few uses. It feels sturdy in the hand, and the build quality seems durable enough to handle being tossed in a backpack or truck bed without falling apart. The price point is also very competitive when you compare it to major brand names that charge twice as much for similar specifications. It delivers exactly what it promises without any hidden fees or complicated setups right out of the box. However, I do have to mention the power switch. It feels a bit flimsy compared to the rest of the unit. It lacks a satisfying click and seems like it could break if you are not careful when flipping it on and off. I have learned to treat it gently, but for the average user who might just want a quick on and off, it might feel too fragile. Despite this questionable switch design, the performance is so solid that I can easily overlook it. For anyone needing a reliable, fast, and affordable pump for sports gear, this is a fantastic choice that earns its five stars.

title: Modern pulp SciFi, with a lot of fun
text: This book is a throwback to the good old days of scifi, with lots of weird aliens, some (fairly) heroic protagonists and a (sort of) quest. The characters are well-drawn, and individual, but they are archetypal, the quest is rather mundane but needed, and the world building is relatively believable. The biggest difference from the earlier pulp fiction is that humans are the least and most recent of the members of the governing Galactic Commons (the GC) with other aliens having much better technology, more advanced civilizations, and a bigger impact on the universe. Humans are acceptable, but it is obvious we are often just tolerated in this world. It is a different take, and an interesting one. I liked the people, I enjoyed the story, and the exciting bits were fine. There is not a lot of back story on how humans became a part of the GC, or what happened to Earth and why humans came to be wandering around seeking a new home, or how they were discovered by the aliens; it is a given from the start. The nine member crew of the Wayfarer contains 5 humans, the owner, two techs (one mechanical, one comp), a clerk, and a fuel specialist (algae is used, and it requires a full-time person to monitor the vats to keep it going); three alien members, a reptile pilot, a bug-like medic/chef, and a fur-covered navigator; and a sapient AI that basically runs the ship. The interactions of the crew and their friends make up much of the book, with some of their backgrounds giving more history. It is a fun read, and I enjoyed it, I was also pleased that there were going to be other books in the series. If you enjoyed the good old days, read this book.

Customer service was also excellent when I had a question about care instructions, but I must admit, I might not need them much since the product is so durable. If you are on the fence about buying this tee, do yourself a favor and pull the trigger. It is rare to find a product that delivers on comfort, durability, and style all at once, but this one does. title: Useless for techies
text:
I'm a developer building a company-internal website and I'm struggling to organize all the information it will contain. I bought this book hoping to ease that struggle. What I found is for a technical person like me, this book was so useless that it has compelled me to write my first Amazon review in years.

I planned to read it cover to cover. After 50 pages I realized that I haven't really read anything at all yet. So far it's been ridiculously verbose, rambling, and content-free. So I gave up and started skimming.

I couldn't find much better in the remaining pages. Page after page of touchy-feely gobbledygook that has not helped me organize information at all.

There are more useless diagrams in this book than I've ever seen before. For example, the term "synonym ring" is defined as a group of words with the same meaning. Does it really take a diagram with a bunch of arrows in a circle to explain that? (Figure 9-2)

To explain the concept of equivalence we have another diagram: "A=B" inside a circle. (Figure 9-21) Does such a diagram really enhance anybody's understanding of the concept of equivalence? Why does this diagram even exist in the first place?

Maybe some business or consultant type might get something out of this book. For a developer, run away. Fast.

text:
Have a Roku TV that is supposed to be wireless-only (why can't they include an rj45 jack anyway?). Even with a wireless router positioned right behind it, still had problems with adaptive streaming sites changing resolution streams multiple times during playback. Searched Roku forums and found an older Belkin adapter mentioned, but that's not available, and has a replacement listed that did not work for me. My son had purchased an HDE adapter for his Wii some time ago (and neglected to tell me), so I tried that and it did work with my TV. so I got one of those, too. Don't know if it was just defective, but the new one didn't work, neither on my TV or the Wii, or even on a laptop, so back it went. Still searching, because I proved to myself that something could work. Finally found this brand mentioned as working after another search, even though the seller says it doesn't. At this point, for $12 I figured what the heck. And it worked... With the other adapters not working I had tried everything, resetting to original settings, unplugging and re-plugging power, USB slot, Cat 6 cable, nothing.

With this adapter, all I had to do was unplug the power cord after installing, plug it back in, turn it on, and it worked. A little slower initial boot, but that's pretty minor to have a working wired connection with no more adaptive streaming fluctuations. Before, Netflix thought i only had 4 Mbps down on a good day, and afterward, that had tripled (according to the test in their app). With another separate speed test app, I'm actually getting as high as 54 Mbps down (out of 60 possible) now.

Edit, 6 weeks later, still using it every day, still working fine except for one incident where it didn't connect after a power on, but I just removed power again and restarted, and has been OK since.

Unfortunately, my experience has been nothing short of disappointing, particularly regarding the build quality. After only three months of careful, normal use, I noticed small but noticeable cracks appearing on both bottom corners of the chassis. This is not a result of any drops or impacts; the laptop sat securely in my bag, which is lined with protective padding, yet the aluminum casing simply gave way under minimal stress. It seems the structural integrity of the bottom case is severely compromised, making this device far less robust than its predecessor or even other laptops in this price range. For a product that costs over a thousand dollars, I expected a level of durability that withstands everyday commuting and handling without falling apart. I have since contacted Apple Support, but the repair process is tedious and the incident feels like a design flaw rather than a random manufacturing defect. It is frustrating to invest in premium hardware only to watch it deteriorate so quickly. I cannot recommend this model to anyone who values longevity or build quality. If you are looking for a reliable machine that won’t show signs of wear and tear in just a few months, I would strongly advise looking elsewhere. title: Exceeded My Expectations In Every Way!
text:
Reign of Shadows exceeded my expectations in every way and kept me on my toes the entire story. Danger around every corner, romance, and adventure had me loving every second of Reign of Shadows. I was seriously hooked until the last sentence, and I defiantly did not want it to end there. Luna is an exceptional heroine in this novel, even with her disadvantages she is stronger and tougher than most of the other survivors left in her world. I could not help but want to root for her in every way.

There is a bit of romance, and I love that it does not come out forced as sometimes I find other book will do just to have a romance aspect to the story. It has a natural feeling to it, and it even acts like a beacon of hope in a world of eternal darkness. With switching points-of-view, readers get to experience the story from both Luna’s perspective and Fowler’s perspective. I have always been a fan of the multiple viewpoint stories, as I think it provides a 360 view of the story and the characters. I think it is a needed feature in Reign of Shadows as these two characters both have many thoughts and secrets that only readers get to experience through the changing perspective.

The setting and world building of Reign of Shadows is perfect. It is a dark and creepy world where dark dwellers rise up from the ground every day to eat anything living and without any real sunlight, survivors of the eclipse on get one hour of peace when the dark is just bright enough to drive the dwellers back underground. The description of the dwellers were detailed enough to nearly give me nightmares after reading Reign of Shadows.

This is the first book of Sophie Jordan’s that I have had the chance to read, but I have always heard amazing things about her other books. Now I know that I have definitely been missing out, and I am setting to rectify that mistake as soon as possible. Her writing sucks you deep in the story and holds you there until the very end brings you back to reality. Only the truly best stories can offer that type of hold over a reader.

title: Hair needed a GOOD wash
text:
I purchased this item last month because my daughter has curly hair that tends to get quite tangled and dry after swimming at the local community pool. The product description claimed it was specifically designed to remove chlorine and salt buildup while maintaining the natural moisture barrier of the hair shaft. I was skeptical at first because there are so many shampoo bottles on the market with similar sounding benefits, but I decided to give it a try since the ratings were generally positive and the price point was reasonable compared to high-end salon brands.

The first thing I noticed upon opening the bottle was the scent. It is not overly floral or fruity, which I appreciate. It smells more like a fresh, clean ocean breeze with a hint of mint. It is refreshing and not overpowering, which is important because strong perfumes often linger in hair for days and can be headache-inducing for some people. I let my daughter wash her hair with this product twice a week for the past three weeks, and I have noticed a significant improvement in the manageability of her curls. They feel softer and the definition is much better than when I used our previous brand.

However, I am only giving it four stars instead of five because of the lather. It does not produce as much foam as I expected. For someone who is used to the heavy, dense bubbles from conventional shampoos, this might feel like it is not actually cleaning her hair. I had to apply a larger amount than I normally would to get the feeling of a thorough cleanse. It is not a dealbreaker, but it is something to be aware of. Additionally, while the bottle is durable, the pump mechanism is a bit stiff and requires a bit of pressure to dispense the product. It works, but it is not as smooth as I would like.

Overall, the performance is excellent. The hair feels genuinely clean without being stripped of natural oils, and the frizz has reduced noticeably. I think this is a solid choice for anyone looking for a gentle, effective wash that respects the integrity of curly or textured hair types. It does what it promises, even if the packaging and lather could be slightly better. I would recommend it to friends who struggle with dry, chlorinated hair, but perhaps suggest they start with a small amount to see how their hair reacts to the lower lather formula. It is a good product, just not perfect.

Been buying these glasses for years. They are cheap, but honestly, they do the job for me. I appreciate that they come in multiple colors, so I can match them to my daily outfits. For the money, you simply cannot beat the value. They are disposable in a sense, but for most people, that is a feature, not a bug. I will continue to buy them because replacement is inexpensive, and they get the job done without breaking the bank. The build quality is surprisingly robust for a toy in this price range. The treads grip well on both carpet and hardwood, which means it actually moves where you want it to go rather than getting stuck under the sofa legs every two seconds.

The sound effects are a nice touch without being overwhelmingly loud or annoying to adults. It plays the classic theme song and has a few explosion noises that really sell the immersive experience for the kids. The remote control is intuitive enough for a child to use independently after just a few minutes of practice, which was a huge bonus. I also appreciate that the opening mechanism for the rear cargo area works smoothly; it allows easy access to the four original action figures, which fits snugly inside. We did have to buy new batteries immediately, as the included ones were likely just for display, but that is standard practice. Assembly was minimal—just snapping on the treads and putting batteries in the shell. It is a fantastic gift option that offers genuine play value rather than just being a static display piece. If you are looking for a durable, engaging toy that brings the nostalgia of the cartoon to life, the Shellraiser is worth every penny. My nephew’s joy when he opened it was priceless, and that alone makes the purchase a success. Highly recommended for any young ninja turtle fan.

I purchased this chew toy expecting it to be a durable, long-lasting solution for my energetic tabby, but it turned out to be a complete waste of money. The scent was also overpowering and artificial, which actually made my cat lose interest in the toy entirely after the initial curiosity wore off. He preferred a crumpled paper ball from the recycling bin over this expensive, poorly designed product. For the price point, I expected much higher quality standards and safety assurances. It broke down too quickly, created a mess I didn't need, and failed to engage my pet in any meaningful way. I cannot recommend this to anyone who has a cat with even a moderate bite force. Save your money and buy a reputable brand that actually stands behind their durability claims. This was a disappointing experience from start to finish.

title: Should be called a ‘wet bag’
text:
I am absolutely disgusted with this purchase and feel completely misled by the product description. I bought this item expecting a high-quality, waterproof container for my sports gear, specifically for carrying sweaty towels and damp clothing after intense workouts. Instead, what arrived in the mail is a pathetic excuse for a bag that does exactly what it should not: it leaks. Calling this a proper storage solution is a joke; it should honestly be classified as a "wet bag" in the worst possible sense of the term, meaning it is useless for its primary intended purpose.

The material feels incredibly cheap and flimsy from the moment you take it out of the package. It lacks any structural integrity, making it difficult to stand up on its own, which is a basic requirement for a gym bag. More importantly, the stitching along the seams is incredibly poor. I only used it once, for about thirty minutes while carrying a slightly damp towel and a change of clothes, and by the time I reached my car, water had seeped through the bottom and wet the entire contents of my other bags. This is not just a minor flaw; it is a complete design failure.

Furthermore, the zipper is a nightmare. It constantly gets stuck, requiring a level of patience and force that I never expected to exert on a simple accessory. Halfway through my walk home, the zipper slid down on its own, spilling wet laundry all over the pavement. This is humiliating and inconvenient. I tried to contact the seller to request a refund, citing the obvious defects, but they have been completely unresponsive. It is frustrating to spend money on a product that feels like it was thrown together in a factory with no quality control whatsoever.

Do not waste your hard-earned money on this item. There are countless better alternatives available at the same price point that actually offer true water resistance and durability. I am left with a soggy mess and a bag that is now too damaged to use for even dry storage. If you value your time and your belongings, steer clear of this product. It is not worth the hassle, the disappointment, or the additional cost of cleaning up the mess it inevitably creates. I am giving this one star because it is the minimum allowed, and honestly, if I could give zero stars, I would. The product is fundamentally broken and fails to meet the most basic expectations of a functional sports accessory.
