title: Flyover Nation- A window into our country's soul.
text:
I bought this book as a gift for my father, who has spent his entire adult life working in the industrial Midwest. It was a challenging subject, as his community often feels misunderstood or overlooked by coastal media narratives, but this book handles the topic with such profound empathy and journalistic integrity that it resonated deeply with him. The author does not offer easy answers or cheap political talking points. Instead, he takes the time to truly listen to the people living in the flyover states, capturing their fears, their dignity, and their complex relationship with modern America.

The narrative structure is compelling, weaving personal anecdotes with broader economic and cultural analysis without ever feeling academic or detached. I found myself reading late into the night, genuinely moved by the human stories at the center of the argument. It is rare to find a work that challenges you to think differently without being preachy. My father actually set it down multiple times to reflect on passages, which rarely happens with non-fiction. This is not just a book about politics; it is a testament to the resilience of the American spirit. It has sparked meaningful conversations at our dinner table about topics we usually avoid. If you are looking for a nuanced, heart-wrenching, and ultimately hopeful look at what makes this country tick, this is essential reading. It deserves every star and more for its courage and clarity.

A few of the later stories dragged a bit, losing their momentum before reaching the climax, which pulled down the overall reading experience slightly. However, the prose is generally polished and engaging, with a few standout pieces that lingered in my mind long after I finished them. It’s not a perfect collection, and I wish the Editor had included more diverse voices to truly reflect the title’s promise. Still, for the price, it offers good value. I would recommend this to readers who enjoy literary fiction with a touch of social commentary. It’s a solid, thoughtful read that deserves attention, even if it doesn’t quite reach the heights of greatness. title: This is an important book
text: First of all, I should say that I spent the last 12 years of my career working at a hospital as a Registered Respiratory Therapist, so when I received this book as a present from a friend I was excited to read it. However, after reading it, I was mystified by some of the critical reviews I found on Amazon. As an RT I spent a lot of time with patients who had breathing problems. This included patients with COPD/emphysema and asthma who struggled to breathe. The standard treatment for these conditions is a class of drugs called bronchodilators. Inhaling these drugs can save people who are unable to breathe, but especially the more chronic patients often don't respond as their bodies seem to become immune to the effects of the drugs over time. With these patients, I would often teach them some of the breathing techniques described in this book. Often I had great success in calming these patients (they're panicked because their damaged lungs make it difficult for them to breathe) and getting them to slow down their respiratory rate. I also worked in cardiopulmonary rehab with both patients who were recovering from heart attacks and pulmonary patients. When we exercised I noticed that most of them had forgotten about their diaphragms and were unable to isolated this critical pulmonary muscle during exercise. Mr. Nestor discusses this in the book. By the way, subsequent research based on the Framingham study does correlate decreased Vital Capacity (total lung volume) with increased cardiovascular risk. In any case, this book does not purport to be a medical textbook and many of the stories are anecdotal and not supported by volumes of medical double-blind studies, but I don't believe that it was the author's intent to propose breathing techniques as a way to cure diseases like scoliosis or ADHD, or as some sort of panacea for curing all illness. In fact, in the Epilogue he says this. But the book is a fascinating journey through 10+ years of the author's research into a much ignored topic. I believe that we can all benefit from practicing the techniques in this book. In short, I like his advice on the "perfect breath": Breathe in through your nose for about 5.5 seconds, then exhale for 5.5 seconds. Practice this for a few minutes. To your health!

title: Weak mechanism leads to snacking for pets
text:
Our cats get very verbal in the wee hours clamoring for us to feed them, so we decided to let them worship a machine instead. This product seems like a great idea, but if your cat has ANY ability to relate cause and effect, it will not work. We have two cats and purchased two feeders. The product functions fine, however, with the slightest bump it distributes more food. Our smarter cat didn't even have to try. After seeing more food was to be had, he stuck his paw right up and was rewarded. We tried putting cardboard over the mouth of the bowl to make it too far for him to reach, but he could still bump it, even when drinking out of his separate water dish! Sitting at home, the feeder would also, completely at random, dispense food, which would of course get the cats all excited. The smarter cat was not only getting rewards for bumping (or hopping on to) the feeders (yes, both), he was getting random snacks. The plastic spindles that meter the food are weak and ineffective. We will be returning these feeders and looking for something less snack-happy.

On the plus, the feeding mechanism was very quiet and easy to program.

title: A Childhood Memory
text:
I had recently read this book because of a Creative Writing assignment. The reason I chose this book is because reading it took me way back to when my mind was early in the stage of the exploration of literature. I owned this book as a child, and reading it gave me another small perspective on how our own life and time itself progresses.

Robert Munsch uses humour in alot of his books and this is another one of those cases. For example, at the end of this book, the child's father is suspended in the middle of the kitchen by his toe with a long rope.

Munsch also uses a form of anticipation to ensure that the child >wants< to turn to the next page. For example, most of the pages in this book have sentences that end like: "He looked in the kitchen, it was empty. He looked in the bathroom, it was empty. He looked in the garage and..."

Not only can I look at this book from the perspective of just an ordinary reader, but also as a child; the intended audience of this book. Because of this, I can say the Robert Munsch did a wonderful job of creating literature that will intrigue children for many future generations

title: No effect what so ever
text: I am absolutely horrified and disgusted by how useless this product is. I cannot believe I actually took the time to write a review, because usually I am too tired to deal with these failures, but this situation is just too egregious to ignore. I bought this item specifically because my dog, Barnaby, has had severe anxiety issues for the past three years. We have tried everything. We have tried the prescription medications that made him lethargic and unkempt. We have tried the expensive, heated orthopedic beds that he refused to sleep on anyway. We have tried the calming sprays that smelled like expired lemon pledge and just confused him. This product was the last hope before I actually had to start carrying sedatives in my pocket every time I took him to the vet or the park. The marketing promised "instant results," "professional-grade tranquility," and "peace of mind for both pet and owner." Let me assure you, there was none of that. There was not even one percent of that. I set it up exactly as the instructions said. I turned the dial to the highest setting. I waited. I watched him closely for any sign of relaxation, for his breathing to slow down, for his ears to stop twitching at the sound of a leaf falling outside. Nothing happened. He sniffed it for approximately three seconds, looked at me with what I can only describe as pure judgment, and then proceeded to bark at a squirrel for another forty-five minutes. It was the same bark he has been doing since 2019. The noise was not dampened. The anxiety was not alleviated. I even held the device near his face, just to see if there was some magical ingredient or frequency I was missing. He sneezed. That was it. A single, annoyed sneeze. I am now out fifty dollars for a piece of plastic that does absolutely nothing. It is a light-up paperweight at best. I feel cheated. I feel like the company is running a scam on desperate pet owners who just want their animals to be happy. Do not waste your money. Do not waste your time. Save your cash and buy Barnaby a really good treat instead, because that will at least make him forget his anxiety for a brief second, which this garbage failed to do for even a fraction of a millisecond. I am returning this immediately. I hope the seller charges me a restocking fee, though honestly, I would pay them to take it back and destroy it so it never harms another pet owner’s wallet again.

I recently finished reading this little book about the Norman conquest of England almost a millenia ago. I found this book interesting, and well written. The author was a former British Naval officer, and he is obviously pro-British, which did not mater to me one way or another.
By genetics, I am part English, and completely Western European, and I read this book to better understand my people's history pre-America. I enjoyed Howarth's take on village life of the commoners/peasantry int he first chapter; he details their low stress, and deep sense of belonging and racial/English community. Written 40 years ago, in a story with no non-Whites, it was still acceptable to talk about racial/tribal community as a natural and healthy thing. title: Birthday gift
text:
I purchased this item as a birthday present for my nephew, who is an avid cyclist and spends most of his weekends on local trails. The packaging arrived in decent condition, with no obvious damage to the box, which was a relief. However, once I opened it to inspect the product itself, I noticed several issues that have left me feeling somewhat indifferent about the overall quality. The material feels thinner than what was advertised, and upon closer inspection, I spotted minor stitching irregularities along the seams. While these defects do not immediately compromise the structural integrity, they certainly raise questions about the product's long-term durability, especially given that it is marketed for rugged outdoor use.

The design is undeniably sleek, and the color options are vibrant, which is why my nephew was initially excited when he opened it. He appreciated the multiple compartments and the water-resistant claim, which seemed practical for his needs. That said, after using it for just two short trips, the zipper began to stick occasionally, requiring some effort to close properly. This is a frustrating issue for a product at this price point, as convenience is a primary selling point for gear used in active lifestyles. Furthermore, the adjustable straps, while functional, feel slightly flimsy and do not secure as tightly as I would expect, leading to a bit of shifting when the bag is fully loaded.

On the positive side, the delivery was prompt, and the customer service team was responsive when I inquired about the warranty terms. It is clear that the brand puts effort into marketing and logistics, but the manufacturing execution leaves something to be desired. I cannot in good conscience recommend this as a top-tier choice for serious outdoor enthusiasts, but for casual use or as a secondary accessory, it might suffice. For the price, I expected a more robust build quality that could withstand regular wear and tear without showing signs of strain so quickly. It is not a bad product by any means, but it does not fully deliver on its promises of durability and ease of use. I hope future iterations improve the stitching and hardware quality, as the current model feels like a cost-cutting measure rather than a genuine upgrade for sports and outdoor activities.

text: I rarely take the time to write reviews, but I felt compelled to do so after finishing this book. I picked it up on a whim during a rainy afternoon, expecting perhaps a lightweight weekend read that I would finish in a single sitting. I was completely wrong. This book demanded my full attention from the very first page and kept me engaged until the final word. It is rare to find a work that manages to be both intellectually stimulating and emotionally resonant at the same time, but the author has achieved something truly special here. The writing style is crisp and unpretentious, yet it carries a weight and depth that lingers in your mind long after you have closed the cover. I found myself pausing frequently to reflect on the themes presented, questioning my own assumptions and seeing the world through a slightly different lens. The characters were not merely vessels for the plot; they felt like real people with complex motivations, flaws, and dreams. You root for them, you despair for them, and you celebrate their victories as if they were your own. The pacing was impeccable. There were moments of high tension that kept me turning pages late into the night, balanced beautifully with quieter, more introspective scenes that allowed for breathing room and deeper connection. I appreciated that the author did not shy away from difficult topics, handling them with nuance and care. It is easy to write about life in the abstract, but it is much harder to capture the raw, messy reality of human experience with such authenticity and grace. This book does not offer easy answers or neat resolutions. Instead, it invites you to sit with the ambiguity and find meaning in the journey itself. For anyone who loves reading but feels like they have read everything, this is a reminder of why we love the medium in the first place. It is a story that matters. It is a story that stays with you. I have already recommended it to several friends and family members, and I can’t wait to discuss it with my book club. If you are on the fence, do yourself a favor and just buy it. You will not be disappointed. This is not just a good book; it is an excellent read that deserves a spot on your shelf and in your heart. Thank you to the author for sharing this gift with us. The second part is dedicated to the effect this deathhas on his victims. As usual in Rendell's novels, we are exposed to her much praised talent to draw in fine psycological detail her charcaters. Because of that, Rendell's novels carry some form of social significance that take them beyond the mystery level. And as usual, this book is a page turner.
However, in this particular novel, she has too many characters and, respectively, too many social issues/implications going on that do not always come together as planned. We have a gay MP that is relevied when he is forced to come out (social responsibiltry vs. personal freedom), his wife who is not necessarily a bad mother to her kids, but still really dumb (feminist ideas vs. traditional upbringing dilemmas); a couple with opposite eating disorders that somehow get cured abd their relationship with their friend who unvoluntarily implcates them in a crime (friednship and betrayal); and all of the above are not related too much to the mystery. I just felt that she has tried to put everything into a single book leaving a lot of the questions she raises unresolved...

The product description promised durability, mental stimulation, and hours of engaging playtime, which sounded too good to be true. After using it for about three weeks, I feel compelled to share my honest experience to help other pet owners make an informed decision.

First, let’s address the build quality. On one hand, the material feels sturdy and the design is intuitive enough for a dog to understand quickly. Buster picked it up in less than five minutes, which was impressive. He spends a good amount of time trying to get the treats out, and that alone has kept him occupied while I work from home. The Kong-like shape is effective for freezing treats, which adds an extra layer of engagement during hot summer days. From a utility standpoint, it does exactly what it claims to do regarding keeping a pet busy and distracted from household furniture.

However, there are notable downsides that prevent this product from earning a five-star rating in my book. The main issue is the cleanup process, which is unnecessarily complicated. It has many small crevices and seams where food particles get trapped. No matter how much I scrub it with hot soapy water, I still worry about bacteria buildup or that strange smell that sometimes lingers after washing. This is a significant drawback for a product that is supposed to be a daily staple in your home. Additionally, while Buster loves it, he has managed to crack a small section after a particularly aggressive play session, despite the claims of being "indestructible." It hasn’t broken apart completely, but it has raised concerns about its long-term durability for powerful chewers.

For light to moderate chewers who are willing to put in the extra effort to clean it thoroughly, this might be a decent option. It offers good value for the price point and provides the mental enrichment that dogs need. However, if you have a heavy-duty destroyer like mine, or if you simply do not have the time to meticulously clean complex toys, you might want to look elsewhere. It is a decent product overall, but it lacks the polish and robustness that would make it a true household essential. I would recommend it with caveats, not as a blanket endorsement for every dog owner.

title: A real treat to Adrien and Jake fans, and a love letter from Josh Lanyon to these beloved characters.
text:
A very entertaining, thought-provoking, occasionally emotional read.

Fatal Shadows, the first book in the Adrien English series, being so well known to Josh’s readers, seemed like the perfect choice for a Choose Your Own Adventure version, because the characters and their original trajectory are so familiar that it becomes easy for readers to experiment with and explore even the wildest alternative scenarios,
The book also presents some new characters and some unexpectedly tender moments involving them,
Moreoever, some of the most satisfying storylines in this book are IMO those where a little more is subtly revealed of a character’s emotion and thought than in the original book. It has a liberating effect, as the CYOA concept allows a lot of freedom to uncover all those fears or bottled up emotions that in the original Fatal Shadows had remained under the surface,
The illustrations by Catherine Dair are the icing on the cake :). They make the book richer (and only a print edition could do them justice) and it’s a nice nod to the original CYOA book format which includes illustrations. And they’re not just there for decoration: Josh uses them as a plot device, so they can’t definitely be missed :)

All in all, I didn't expect such a rich and inventive book. What I did expect, and was not disappointed with, was the apparently effortless way Josh Lanyon has to combine humour, dry wit and emotion in such a creative and satisfying way.

text:
I was genuinely excited to try this product after reading the glowing reviews and seeing the impressive marketing claims. It promised durability, comfort, and an easy setup process, which seemed like exactly what I needed for my energetic golden retriever. I spent the afternoon assembling it, following the instructions carefully, and everything seemed to fit together perfectly at first glance. It looked sturdy on my hardwood floors, and my dog gave it a quick sniff before ignoring it for a few hours. That quiet period, however, was short-lived. By the next morning, the structural integrity was already compromised. One of the main support legs had snapped right at the base, despite me not applying any excessive force or weight. I didn’t even have my two hundred-pound mastiff near it; it was just sitting there.

The plastic material feels cheap and brittle, not at all like the heavy-duty resin advertised in the description. When I tried to tighten the loose connections, the threads stripped completely, rendering the entire assembly useless. I reached out to customer support, expecting some level of assistance given the obvious defect, but was met with a generic email asking for more photos. It has been three days, and I still haven’t heard back. For a product at this price point, I expected at least a week of usage before any signs of wear, let alone catastrophic failure. It is incredibly frustrating to buy something that is supposed to make pet care easier, only to have it become another piece of clutter in my garage. I cannot recommend this to anyone who wants something reliable. Save your money and invest in a brand with a better reputation for quality control. My dog is currently happier with an old, worn-out toy that has lasted years, rather than this shiny new disaster that fell apart before I even finished my morning coffee.

title: Great customer service added two stars!

UPDATE:

I have added two stars to this drone review. The customer service from Dynalog is outstanding. They got the app working with my phone. At the time I am writing this update, downloading the app using the QR code failed for me. However, you search the app store for Dynalog Casper and download the app there, you hopefully will have the same success as I did. After connecting my phone to the drone's wifi and starting the app, I had video from the drone. I was able to record video and take photos. After playing with this drone, I can say that it is a great starter drone to get your feet wet in the world of flying drones. I can now definitely recommend this as a great starter drone for anyone.

Original review below:

This is really a neat little drone. It is amazing all of the features that this tiny little drone has. It comes with two batteries to keep you flying longer and even two usb chargers for each battery. Included is another full set of propellers and screws. The remote has nice one-touch built in functions. It all around the drone is fun to play with.

However, here is the deal breaker. The app is not supported by my phone. I have a Samsung S21 5G phone. When I scanned the QR code in the quick start manual, the APP indicates that it is not compatible with my phone. Another reviewer has mentioned that their phone was not compatible with the app either. The point of having a drone is to view and record video from the flight. Without this feature, there is no point in owning the drone.

The hardware is great, but the software evidentially is still in the development stage. Keep shopping. You will be disappointed in this one. I will change my review should software for this drone ever be developed for a larger base of phones.

I had seen a few other options on the market that promised similar mechanics but were significantly more expensive, and I didn’t want to spend a fortune just to see if my family would actually enjoy it. The first thing I noticed upon opening the box was the quality of the components. The pieces feel sturdy and well-made, not flimsy like some cheaper alternatives I have tried in the past. We played our first session last weekend with some friends, and the learning curve was surprisingly gentle. It struck a nice balance between casual fun and tactical depth, which meant that both the competitive gamer in our group and the more laid-back players felt included and entertained. There were plenty of moments of laughter and friendly debate, which is exactly what I look for when gathering people together.

For the price point, this is an absolute steal. I have played games that cost three times as much that were not nearly as fun or well-designed. This game offers tremendous value for money. It is versatile enough to be played with small groups or larger parties, and the replayability factor is high because no two games seem to play out exactly the same way. If you are on the fence about buying this, do not hesitate. It is a fantastic addition to any game night collection, offering hours of entertainment without breaking the bank. I have already recommended it to several other friends and family members, and I anticipate buying a second copy for my parents soon. If you're packing the keyboard in a bag, make sure to pack it close to something that will give it support, as it's quite thin and would probably flex and get damaged if just carelessly tossed in a bag with a bunch of other stuff.

Some other reviewers said that the keyboard slides around if put on a desk. Mine came with stick-on rubber feet (included in the box) that solved the sliding problem.

What truly sets this apart is the educational value it provides. It isn’t just a distraction; it actually encourages problem-solving skills and fine motor development in a way that feels organic and fun. I have purchased this exact set a second time for my niece’s birthday, and I plan to buy more as her friends come over. The customer service was also exceptional when I had a minor question about assembly, with a representative responding within hours. For parents who are tired of buying cheap plastic gadgets that break after a week, this is a worthwhile investment. It keeps my child engaged for hours, which is a miracle in itself.
